result:
Before I write it up, one bigger choice is still open: how the guide is put together as a whole, and in particular how a volunteer gets a recording from their phone into it. Here are the three realistic ways, building on your existing Eleventy site on Netlify where it makes sense:

1. **Everything inside the website.** Each exhibit gets a guide page on the current site, and the audio files live alongside the site's pages. Volunteers upload through a simple editing screen added to the site, and the cleanup runs automatically when the site rebuilds. This has the fewest new pieces. But 120 recordings, growing every year, make the site heavy and slow to rebuild, and those editing screens are awkward on a phone.

2. **Guide pages on the website, recordings stored separately.** The guide pages still live on your site. The audio sits in separate file storage built for it. Volunteers use a small sign-in page, made for phones, to upload a recording for an exhibit and language. The cleanup runs on each upload, and the new version replaces the old one. This adds a couple of new pieces to look after, but it suits audio and phone uploads well.

3. **An existing audio-guide service** (Smartify and izi.TRAVEL are examples). They already handle scanning, languages and uploads, so there's almost nothing to build. The catch is that automatic levelling and trimming generally aren't offered, so you'd lose the cleanup you just chose. The guide would also live on their platform rather than yours.

I recommend **2**. It keeps the cleanup and gives volunteers an upload made for phones. It also means each code beside an exhibit points at a page address that never changes, so replacing a recording never means reprinting a code.

This is a project rather than a small change, so I'll write it as a full design document in the website's repo. A reviewer will read it before I hand it over, and I may come back once with a few questions.

Which way do you want to go?
